n8e083ab8699.s: Which of the following about Akbar's religious measures is NOT correct?
o: The Ibadat Khana was built in 1575.
The Mahzar preceded the construction of the Ibadat Khana.
n8e083ab8699.x: The Mahzar (1579) came after the Ibadat Khana (1575); the order is jizya abolished 1564, Ibadat Khana 1575, Mahzar 1579, Din-i-Ilahi 1582.

nindian-history-18-2.s: Aurangzeb's first coronation, held at Delhi, took place on:
nindian-history-18-2.x: Aurangzeb was first crowned at Delhi on 21 July 1658, before Deorai; his second coronation was on 5 June 1659 after Khajwa and Deorai.

n9c132a2a61b.s: The capital of Banda Singh Bahadur's Sikh state was:
n9c132a2a61b.x: Banda Singh Bahadur's capital was Lohgarh; Anandpur Sahib was founded by Guru Tegh Bahadur.

nef61b73c9fc.s: Todar Mal's revenue arrangements built upon the earlier survey-based system of:
nef61b73c9fc.x: Todar Mal had earlier served Sher Shah and built upon Sher Shah's survey-based system.

nc80fd84e019.s: Which of the following about the state share under Todar Mal's revenue arrangement is NOT correct?
o: It was one-third of the average produce.
It was normally paid in cash called dam.
Payment in kind was allowed in some areas.
It was paid in cash called jital.
nc80fd84e019.x: The state share was paid in cash called dam, not jital, though payment in kind was allowed in some areas.

na289a7fc6ca.s: Under the Qutb Shahis of Golconda, the state generally took what share of the produce?
na289a7fc6ca.x: Golconda generally took one-third of the produce, not one-half.

n7379ba25e8c.s:
Consider the following statements about the battles of the war of succession:
1. Bahadurgarh was fought before Dharmat.
2. Samugarh was fought before Khajwa.
3. Deorai was the first battle of the war.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n7379ba25e8c.x: The order was Bahadurgarh, Dharmat, Samugarh, Khajwa and Deorai (February 1658 to March 1659), so Deorai was the last battle, not the first.

new.s: Akbar personally killed Adham Khan in 1562 for murdering:
new.x: Adham Khan, son of Maham Anaga, was killed by Akbar in 1562 for murdering Atagh Khan.

new.s: Akbar was born in 1542 at:
new.x: Akbar was born on 15 October 1542 at Amarkot; Kalanaur is where he was crowned in 1556.

new.s: Akbar annexed Kashmir in 1586 from:
new.x: Kashmir was taken in 1586 from Yusuf Shah Chak; Miran Bahadur was of Khandesh and Baz Bahadur of Malwa.

new.s: Akbar's capture of Ahmednagar in 1600 was resisted by:
new.x: Chand Bibi defended Ahmednagar (1600); Rani Durgavati resisted in Gondwana (1564).

new.s: Which of the following pairs (Region – opponent of Akbar) is correctly matched?
new.x: Ranthambore (1569) was held by Surjan Rai Hada; Malwa was Baz Bahadur's, Bengal Daud Khan's, Kabul Mirza Hakim's and Khandesh Miran Bahadur's.

new.s: Akbar abolished the pilgrimage tax in:
new.x: The pilgrimage tax was abolished in 1563 and jizya in 1564.

new.s: Which ruler abolished the grain tax?
new.x: The grain tax was ended by Sikandar Lodi, not Akbar.

new.s: In Islamic taxation, 'Khums' meant:
new.x: Khums was one-fifth of war booty; Ushr was land tax, Zakat alms tax and Haqq-e-Sharb irrigation tax.

new.s: Din-i-Ilahi had about how many members?
new.x: Din-i-Ilahi was a small voluntary circle of about 18 members.

new.s: Who is regarded as the chief exponent ('prophet') of Din-i-Ilahi?
new.x: Abul Fazl was its chief exponent; Badauni and Ahmad Sirhindi were its orthodox critics.

new.s: Akbar conferred the title 'Yuga Pradhan' on the Jain scholar:
new.x: Jinachandra Suri was called Yuga Pradhan; Hiravijaya Suri received the title Jagat Guru.

new.s: The Parsi priest who received a land grant from Akbar was:
new.x: Dastur Meherji Rana, a Parsi, received a land grant; Xavier and Acquaviva were Jesuits.

new.s: The second Jesuit mission from Goa reached Akbar's court in:
new.x: The Jesuit missions came in 1580, 1591 and 1595; 1591 was the second.

new.s: Akbar's translation bureau at Fatehpur Sikri was called:
new.x: The Maktab Khana ('House of Translation') was Akbar's translation bureau; the Ibadat Khana was the hall of religious debate.

new.s: Akbar's Maktab Khana was set up around:
new.x: The Maktab Khana was set up at Fatehpur Sikri around 1574.

new.s: Who translated the Yogavasistha into Persian under Akbar?
new.x: Nizamuddin Panipati translated the Yogavasistha; Abdur Rahim translated the Baburnama.

new.s: The Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri commemorates Akbar's conquest of:
new.x: The Buland Darwaza marks the Gujarat conquest of 1572-73.

new.s: Which of the following about Fatehpur Sikri is NOT correct?
o: The Buland Darwaza there commemorates the conquest of Bengal.
The Ibadat Khana was built there in 1575.
The first Jesuit mission reached it in 1580.
new.x: The Buland Darwaza commemorates the Gujarat conquest (1572-73), not Bengal.

new.s: Raja Birbal was killed in 1586 while fighting the:
new.x: Birbal was killed in 1586 fighting the Yusufzai.

new.s: The dual ranks of Zat and Sawar in Akbar's mansabdari date from about:
new.x: Zat and Sawar dual ranks came about 1595-96; 1573-74 was the Dagh system.

new.s: The du-aspa sih-aspa system was introduced by:
new.x: Du-aspa sih-aspa was Jahangir's measure, first for Mahabat Khan; Zat-Sawar was Akbar's.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the mansabdari system:
1. It was introduced by Akbar.
2. The Dagh system of horse branding dates from 1573-74.
3. Du-aspa sih-aspa was first granted to Mahabat Khan by Akbar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; du-aspa sih-aspa was introduced by Jahangir, not Akbar.

new.s: Dara Shikoh's Majma-ul-Bahrain brings together:
new.x: Majma-ul-Bahrain ('mingling of two oceans') compares Sufism and Vedanta.

new.s: Dara Shikoh's Sirr-i-Akbar (1657) is a Persian translation of the:
new.x: Sirr-i-Akbar is the Persian Upanishads (1657); the Mahabharata became the Razmnama under Akbar.

new.s: Babur's memoir, the Tuzuk-i-Baburi, was written in:
new.x: Babur wrote in Turki; Jahangir's Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri was in Persian.

new.s: Which Sikh Guru built the Akal Takht?
new.x: Guru Hargobind, the sixth Guru, built the Akal Takht and was imprisoned at Gwalior.

new.s: Akbar's Karori experiment was introduced in:
new.x: The Karori experiment was in 1574; the Dahsala followed in 1580.

new.s: Under the Karori experiment, the officers in charge of the revenue circles were called:
new.x: Each circle yielding one crore dams was under an officer called a karori.

new.s: Akbar's unit of length, the Gaz-i-Ilahi, measured about:
new.x: The Gaz-i-Ilahi was about 82 cm.

new.s: The Dahsala was based on the average produce and prices of the years:
new.x: The Dahsala (1580) used the average of the last ten years, 1571-1580.

new.s: Under the Mughals, Batai (Ghalla-bakhshi) was mainly used in:
new.x: Crop-sharing (batai) was used in Thatta, Kabul and Kashmir; Nasaq was mainly in Bengal and Zabti in the core provinces.

new.s: Under Akbar's land classification, land left uncultivated for five years or more was called:
new.x: Banjar was fallow 5+ years; Parauti 1-2 and Chachar 3-4 years.

new.s: In Akbar's classification, Polaj was land that was:
new.x: Polaj land was cultivated every year.

new.s: Mughal revenue-free grants to scholars, holy men and the needy were called:
new.x: Madad-i-maash (also suyurghal) was a charitable revenue-free grant; Khalisa was crown land.

new.s: The Mughal mansabdari system had its origin in the:
new.x: Mansabdari was of Central Asian / Mongol military origin.

new.s: Under Akbar, mansabs above those of the nobles (5,000, later 7,000) were given only to:
new.x: Noble ranks ran from 10 to 5,000 (later 7,000); higher ranks were only for royal princes.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Akbar's mansabdari system:
1. Zat denoted personal rank and pay.
2. Sawar denoted the number of horsemen to be maintained.
3. Mansabs were hereditary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Zat was personal rank and Sawar the horsemen to be kept; mansabs were non-hereditary.

new.s: A mansabdar whose sawar rank equalled his zat rank was placed in the:
new.x: By the sawar-zat ratio, sawar equal to zat made a mansabdar first class.

new.s: Which type of Mughal jagir was hereditary and not transferable?
new.x: Watan jagir, the zamindar's homeland, was hereditary and not transferable.

new.s: Tankha jagirs, given in lieu of salary, were normally transferred every:
new.x: Tankha jagirs were transferable every 3-4 years, which prevented local power bases.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (Jagir type – feature) is correctly matched?
o: Mashrut – conditional, tied to specified duties
new.x: Mashrut was conditional; Watan was non-transferable, In'am carried no service obligation and Tankha was in lieu of salary.

new.s: Which Mughal central minister handled military matters such as dagh, chehra and promotions?
new.x: The Mir Bakhshi was the military head in charge of dagh, chehra and promotions.

new.s: The Mughal Sadr-us-sudur was in charge of:
new.x: The Sadr-us-sudur dealt with religious affairs, charitable grants and the Shariat.

new.s: Which of the following about Mughal central ministers is NOT correct?
o: The Mir Saman was in charge of religious affairs.
The Wakil was the highest in rank.
The Wazir handled revenue, treasury and accounts.
new.x: The Mir Saman looked after the royal household and karkhanas; religious affairs were with the Sadr-us-sudur.

new.s: Which Mughal official kept the land and revenue records of a pargana?
new.x: The qanungo kept pargana land and revenue records; the potdar was a treasurer.

new.s: In Mughal revenue administration, the Potdar was the:
new.x: The potdar was the treasurer; the patwari was the village accountant and the amalguzar the sarkar revenue collector.

new.s: In 1580, Akbar's empire was divided into how many subas?
new.x: There were 12 subas in 1580.

new.s: Law and order in a Mughal town was the duty of the:
new.x: The kotwal kept law and order in the city; the faujdar did so at sarkar level.

new.s: In 1626, Mahabat Khan seized Jahangir on the bank of the:
new.x: Mahabat Khan's coup of 1626 seized Jahangir on the Jhelum.

new.s: Which of the following did NOT take place in Jahangir's reign?
new.x: Kabul and Kandahar were not annexed by Jahangir; Kandahar was in fact lost to Persia in 1622.

new.s: Prince Khurram's revolt against Jahangir lasted from:
new.x: Khurram revolted in 1622-26 when Nur Jahan backed Shahryar as heir.

new.s: The mother of Prince Khusrau, Jahangir's eldest son, was:
new.x: Khusrau's mother was Man Bai; Jagat Gosain was the mother of Shah Jahan.

new.s: Which Mughal consort had her name placed on coins and farmans?
new.x: Nur Jahan was the only Mughal consort whose name appeared on coins and farmans.

new.s: Before marrying Jahangir, Mehrunnisa (Nur Jahan) was the widow of:
new.x: Mehrunnisa was the widow of Sher Afghan; Asaf Khan was her brother.

new.s: Which member of Nur Jahan's junta was her brother and Shah Jahan's father-in-law?
new.x: Asaf Khan was Nur Jahan's brother and father of Mumtaz Mahal; Itimad-ud-Daulah (Ghiyas Beg) was her father.

new.s: Which French physician was linked with Dara Shikoh and later attended Aurangzeb's court?
new.x: Bernier, a French physician, was linked with Dara and later Aurangzeb; Manucci was a Venetian.

new.s: 'Storia do Mogor' was written by:
new.x: The Venetian Niccolao Manucci, Dara's artilleryman, wrote Storia do Mogor.

new.s: William Hawkins reached Surat in 1608 aboard the ship:
new.x: Hawkins came on the Hector to Surat in 1608 and reached Agra in 1609.

new.s: The first Mughal-British conflict (1686) took place in the reign of:
new.x: In 1686 under Aurangzeb, Shaista Khan drove the English out of Hooghly.

new.s: Dara Shikoh was buried in:
new.x: Dara Shikoh, executed in 1659, was buried in Humayun's Tomb.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (Emperor – son) is correctly matched?
new.x: Murad was Shah Jahan's son; Kamran was Babur's and Khusrau Jahangir's.

new.s: Shah Jahan remained a captive in Agra Fort until his death in:
new.x: Shah Jahan was confined in Agra Fort for about 8 years until his death in 1666.

new.s: Shah Jahan's reign is called the 'golden age' of Mughal:
new.x: Shah Jahan's reign is the golden age of Mughal architecture (Taj Mahal, Lal Qila, Jama Masjid).

new.s: Shah Jahan's Balkh-Badakhshan campaign (1646-47) was led by:
new.x: The Balkh campaign was led by Murad Bakhsh and then Aurangzeb, not Dara, and failed with heavy losses.

new.s: The Mughal siege of Kandahar in 1653, after which it was lost for good, was led by:
new.x: Aurangzeb led the 1649 and 1652 sieges; Dara led the failed 1653 siege.

new.s: When Aurangzeb annexed Bijapur in 1686, its last ruler was:
new.x: Sikandar Adil Shah was the last ruler of Bijapur; Tana Shah was Golconda's.

new.s: Golconda's Inqiyad Nama, placing Shah Jahan's name in the khutba and on coins, was accepted by:
new.x: Abdullah Qutb Shah's Inqiyad Nama put Shah Jahan's name in the khutba and on coins.

new.s: Aurangzeb served as viceroy of the Deccan during:
new.x: Aurangzeb was Deccan viceroy in 1636-44 and 1652-58.

new.s: The Battle of Dharmat (1658) was fought near:
new.x: Dharmat was near Ujjain; Samugarh near Agra, Deorai near Ajmer and Bahadurgarh near Banaras.

new.s: The Battle of Deorai (1659), Dara Shikoh's final defeat, was fought near:
new.x: Deorai was near Ajmer; Khajwa was near Fatehpur.

new.s: After his defeat in the war of succession, Shah Shuja fled to:
new.x: Shuja fled to Arakan; Murad was imprisoned in Gwalior.

new.s: Murad Bakhsh was imprisoned in Gwalior and executed in:
new.x: Murad Bakhsh was imprisoned in Gwalior and executed in 1661.

new.s: The Satnami revolt against Aurangzeb was centred at:
new.x: The Satnamis rose at Narnaul; the Jats at Mathura and Gokula.

new.s: The Rajput resistance to Aurangzeb in Marwar is associated with:
new.x: Durgadas Rathore led the Rajput resistance in Marwar and Mewar.

new.s: Aurangzeb took the title:
new.x: Aurangzeb took the title Alamgir; Shah-i-Iqbal was Dara's title.

new.s: The Jat revolt against Aurangzeb was centred around:
new.x: The Jats rose around Mathura and Gokula.
